title: Scene launch checks the build state: skip the build when target/classes is current, compile only what changed, clean only when needed
definition-of-done:
1. run-scene and launch skip Maven entirely when no input is newer than the last successful build stamp, and say so on one line with the reason.
2. A changed resource only syncs resources; a changed source compiles; a changed annotations module or annotation-processor input, a missing/failed/interrupted build, or a changed pom runs the full clean compile, each with its reason printed.
3. If an incremental ixdar-app compile is used, the generated registries and automation_routes.json are identical to a clean build's (test); if it cannot be made correct, the source-changed case runs the clean compile and the ticket says why.
4. Measured on the main checkout: launch time of a scene with nothing changed, before and after, recorded on the ticket.
5. test_cli covers the decision for each case with a fake tree (no Maven run).
testing-plan:
1. Unit tests in test_cli.py for the decision function over temp trees with chosen mtimes and stamp states.
2. Live: launch a scene twice in a row (second skips the build), touch a resource (sync only), touch a .java (compile), touch an annotations source (clean compile), kill a build midway then launch (clean compile).
3. Compare generated registries and automation_routes.json from an incremental build with a clean build, if incremental is used.
changes-made:
run-scene and launch now decide the build themselves (run_scene.py build_inputs / build_decision, used by _ensure_build for both commands) and print one line, e.g. `build: current (no input changed since the last build at 2026-10-17 12:29:24)`, `build: incremental compile (1 source(s) changed: Shutdown.java)`, `build: clean compile (annotations changed: SceneDrawable.java)`. The stamp is ixdar-app/target/ixdar-cli-build.json (per worktree, removed by any mvn clean): the path and st_mtime_ns of every input (the three poms, annotations/src, ixdar-app/src/main/java, ixdar-app/src/main/resources), taken just before the build, deleted before Maven starts and written only after it succeeds. Inputs compare by exact mtime and by path set, so edits, additions, deletions and a rename that keeps its mtime all count, and a file edited during a build is caught next time. Rules, first match wins: no stamp (never built, failed, interrupted) -> clean compile; ixdar-app/target/classes or annotations/target/classes missing -> clean; a pom changed -> clean; anything under annotations/src changed or removed -> clean; a resource removed -> clean (sync cannot delete stale copies); any java source changed/added/removed -> `mvn compile -pl annotations,ixdar-app` without clean; only resources changed/added -> sync_resources and restamp, no Maven; else current, no Maven. --skip-build still forces a launch of whatever is on disk (sync resources, no stamp change).

Why incremental is safe (the unknown): on maven-compiler-plugin 3.13.0 (useIncrementalCompilation default true) any stale source makes the plugin recompile the whole module (all 849 files) and delete the outputs of removed sources (maven-status inputFiles.lst), so the five RegistryProcessor subclasses (AutomationRouteRegistry, CommandRegistry, GeometryRegistry, MeshNodeRegistry with its Desktop partition, SceneRegistry) always see every annotated type; nothing is pruned and export-automation-routes runs on a full registry. The pruning the old docstring described could not be reproduced: touching a plain class, an annotated route and an annotated scene, adding a new @AutomationRouteAnnotation class and then deleting it, each compiled without clean, left target/generated-sources/annotations, automation_routes.json, mesh-node-catalog.json and the target/classes file list byte-identical to a clean build's, and the added route appeared in the registry. tools/check-incremental-build.sh repeats that comparison (clean snapshot vs touch + add + remove incremental) and exits non-zero on any diff; run it after changing the compiler plugin or the processors. No processor change was needed. The processor path in the reactor build is annotations/target/classes (mvn -X), so an annotations change still clean-compiles both modules.

Measured on the tool-18 worktree, scene circle-canvas via run-scene with a screenshot, wall time of the whole command: before, nothing changed: 20.0 s (mvn clean compile + CP refresh every launch). After: nothing changed 2.6 s (twice; launch "Circle" also 2.6 s); touched resource 2.6 s (resources only); touched plain .java 12.0 s and touched annotated route 11.7 s (incremental compile); touched annotations source 19.7 s (clean compile); first launch with no stamp 18.8 s (clean); build killed after 5 s (TERM to the process group) left no stamp and the next launch clean-compiled, 19.6 s.

Tests: test_cli.py test_build_decision_covers_every_build_state (15 fake-tree cases: nothing changed, resource edited/added/removed, source edited/older copy/renamed/deleted, annotations edited, app and parent pom, classes and annotations classes deleted, stamp deleted or truncated, no stamp) and test_ensure_build_stamps_only_a_build_that_succeeded (a failed Maven leaves no stamp; a success stamps and the next call runs no Maven). unittest: 93 run, 1 failure that is on master already (test_screenshot_and_frame_routes_expose_their_new_flags: the frame route gained point/radius/region/ring). mvn test: 505 run, 0 failures. tools/check-incremental-build.sh: matches.
